subject: Biotechnology
title: HLA and Drug Hypersensitivity
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on HLA and Drug Hypersensitivity.

hook.text: Abacavir treats HIV — but in 5% of patients it triggers a life-threatening allergic reaction. One gene test prevents it.

buildup.text: HLA-B*57:01 presents abacavir fragments to T cells as if they were foreign — triggering a massive immune attack.

discovery.text: Mandatory HLA testing before prescribing abacavir virtually eliminated hypersensitivity reactions — a pharmacogenomic triumph.

twist.text: Carbamazepine and HLA-B*15:02 cause Stevens-Johnson syndrome — severe skin blistering, especially common in Southeast Asians.

climax.text: Pre-prescription HLA testing is now standard for several drugs — genotype before the first pill.

punchline.text: One test, zero deadly reactions — HLA screening is pharmacogenomics at its best.

quiz.question: How does HLA-B*57:01 cause abacavir hypersensitivity?
options: It prevents the body from absorbing abacavir properly
It presents abacavir fragments to T cells, triggering an immune attack as if they were foreign
It converts abacavir into a toxic metabolite in the liver

details.summary: Human leukocyte antigen variants are strongly associated with severe drug hypersensitivity reactions including Stevens-Johnson syndrome and drug-induced liver injury. Pre-treatment HLA testing can prevent life-threatening adverse reactions to drugs like carbamazepine, abacavir, and allopurinol.
details.whyItMatters: Severe drug hypersensitivity reactions kill or permanently injure thousands of patients annually. HLA testing before prescribing high-risk drugs is one of pharmacogenomics' greatest successes, preventing potentially fatal reactions with a simple
takeaways: Specific HLA alleles predict severe drug hypersensitivity with high accuracy
HLA-B*57:01 testing before abacavir virtually eliminated hypersensitivity reactions
Pre-treatment testing is mandated or recommended for several high-risk drugs

faq.question: How does HLA typing prevent drug reactions?
faq.answer: Certain HLA proteins present drug molecules to immune cells in a way that triggers massive immune attacks against the patient's own tissues. Testing for the specific HLA allele before prescribing identifies at-risk patients. Alternative drugs are chosen, completely avoiding the reaction.

faq.question: Which drug-HLA associations are clinically implemented?
faq.answer: HLA-B*57:01 testing before abacavir is mandatory. HLA-B*15:02 testing before carbamazepine is recommended for Southeast Asian patients. HLA-B*58:01 testing before allopurinol is increasingly adopted. Each association was validated by clinical trials showing testing eliminated severe reactions.
